Package io.thymekit

Class Element<K>

java.lang.Object
io.thymekit.Element<K>
All Implemented Interfaces:
Composable<K>
public final class Element<K> extends Object implements Composable<K>
The single currency of composition: every element's build() returns one. Elements go onto a canvas (PageModel), into containers and into larger elements.

K is a phantom marker — the factory class that produced the element (Element<Heading>). There is no type hierarchy: a new element is just a factory, and the type it produces exists for free. Wide points accept Element<?>; narrow points name the marker, so the compiler rejects a combination only where it is genuinely meaningless.

Inside is a descriptor: the address of the element's adapter fragment (template :: fragment(e)) plus data. Templates read asMap(), so the adapter contract does not depend on typing: the data is untyped, the marker is typed.

Five things live in this file, and a reader arriving at it should know which one they are in:

  • the value — asMap(), build(), template(), fragment(), bare(), slot(String), slotNames(), and equality, which is the descriptor's;
  • the maker — Element.Descriptor, the one way an element is made, here and in consumer code, with raw(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) and script(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) as its two shortcuts;
  • the guards a host uses — settle(io.thymekit.Composable<K>, java.lang.String), requireRenderable(io.thymekit.Element<?>, java.lang.String), requireRenderableElement(io.thymekit.Element<?>, java.lang.String), requireAdapter(io.thymekit.Element<?>, java.lang.String, java.lang.String), requireTag(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), all public, because an element of yours hosts other elements the same way the kit's own do;
  • and nothing about trees. What a page or a subtree yields — the scripts it depends on, what its elements say about themselves — is Tree's business, as is every other question whose answer needs more than one element.

Each is specified by a file of its own next to ElementTest. What used to be a fifth thing here — the outline of a page — lives in Outline now: it is a property of a page rather than of an element, and holding it here had taught the currency the name of one element's adapter.

    • required

      public static <T> T required(@Nullable T value, String where)
      A value that had to be given. Replaces Objects.requireNonNull everywhere in the kit: the exception it throws is somebody else's, and a consumer cannot tell it from their own code failing — which is the whole reason this family exists.

    • requireAbsolute

      public static String requireAbsolute(String url, String where)
      An address that leaves the page — into a canonical link, into Open Graph, into a graph a crawler reads — is absolute or it is broken. Whoever reads it is not looking at the document and has nothing to resolve a path against, and the failure is silent: no preview, or a canonical pointing at a stranger.

      Public because two elements need it, and two users make a policy rather than a detail.

    • requireNavigable

      public static String requireNavigable(String href, String where)
      An address that navigates. Kept trimmed, refused when blank, and refused when its scheme executes rather than goes somewhere — javascript:, data:, vbscript:, however they are spelled, since a browser drops spaces, tabs and control characters before reading a scheme and java\tscript: is the plain one by the time it is followed.

      Public because two elements need it, and an href is the last place any of those can be stopped before the page.

    • requireText

      public static String requireText(String text, String where)
      Text a page will show: given, and not empty. Two elements refuse the same thing for the same reason — a caption with nothing in it is an empty box, a heading with nothing in it is a place in the outline a screen reader stops at and finds nothing — so the refusal is one rule in one place rather than two spellings of it.

      What is given is kept exactly: a space inside a line belongs to whoever wrote the line. Only a text that is nothing at all is refused.

    • requireTag

      public static String requireTag(String tag, String where)
      A language tag, the way lang wants it: letters, digits and hyphens, nothing else. Not the full BCP-47 grammar — just enough that a sentence, a translation or an empty string never ends up in the attribute, where it would silently make the page claim a language it does not speak.

      Public with the other guards: two elements of the kit already use it, which makes it the policy of a concept rather than a detail of either, and an element of yours that offers lang needs the same check the kit's own make.

    • settle

      public static <K> Element<K> settle(Composable<K> composable, String where)
      Whatever becomes an element, settled at once and never before: a place that takes a Composable builds it here, keeps the element and forgets the maker. That is the rule the kit follows everywhere — accept what becomes an element, store only what has become one.
